sources: Bulgaria Central Election Commission (CEC/CIK) official runoff count, via Trend.az / APA / Votendi CIK tracker
fault_line: Dialogue-with-Moscow president in a NATO/EU Black Sea state after Black Sea shipping attacks: mandate for peace, or a tilt that worries Brussels and Kyiv?

sections.what_happened: Iliana Iotova + Kiril Valchev: 57.636% (1,077,092 votes); Andrey Gyurov + Georgi Kandev: 39.402% (736,334); 'None of the above': 2.962% (55,353), at 98.43% of polling-station protocols processed (CEC timestamp 03:00 Nov 2). Gyurov conceded on election night ('results have to be accepted as they stood'). EU chief Ursula von der Leyen congratulated Iotova. Formal final results due no later than Nov 4; new term begins Jan 22, 2027. Iotova, 62, acting president who favours dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine, becomes Bulgaria's first elected woman president; the vote was held against October Black Sea commercial-vessel drone strikes (21 missing). Spelling note: Trend.az renders 'Yotova'; CEC/APA/Firstpost use 'Iotova'.
sections.what_verified: CEC primary data republished by Trend.az, APA, Votendi CIK tracker, Firstpost/AFP; Gyurov concession + von der Leyen congratulation reported by multiple outlets.
sections.what_disputed: None on the result; formal certification still pending (due by Nov 4) and 1.57% of protocols unprocessed — neither can overturn an 18.2-point lead. Framing dispute only: outlets label Iotova 'pro-Russia'/'Moscow-friendly' while her stated message was 'incomes, peace and the challenges that lie ahead'.
sections.why_matters: Bulgaria just elected the dialogue candidate by 18 points while its Black Sea shipping is under attack — what that means for NATO's Black Sea flank.
